text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me which specific antibiotic you were prescribed?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of fever, itchy rash, and joint pain starting in the flexor creases (antecubital and popliteal fossae) shortly after taking amoxicillin is highly suggestive of Drug-Induced Hypersensitivity Syndrome. Is there any involvement of your mouth, eyes, or respiratory tract, such as swelling, a sore throat, or difficulty breathing? Also, have you noticed a significant drop in your urine output or a darkening of your urine color?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Liver function tests (AST, ALT, Bilirubin), Creatinine, and Blood Culture.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Maculopapular Drug Eruption (Drug Hypersensitivity). The clinical presentation of an itchy rash starting in the flexor creases and spreading, accompanied by fever and joint pain shortly after amoxicillin initiation, is characteristic of a type IV hypersensitivity reaction.
